# Skill: Tune the decision threshold on OOF probabilities when the metric is F1 / F-beta / MCC

## Precondition
Apply this skill if ALL of the following hold:

1. The task is binary classification (target has exactly 2 classes), AND
2. The headline metric is one of: `f1`, `f1_binary`, `f_beta`, `fbeta`, `mcc`, `matthews`, `balanced_accuracy` (any threshold-sensitive metric — NOT `roc_auc`, NOT `log_loss`, NOT `accuracy` if classes are balanced), AND
3. The chosen model has a `predict_proba` (or `decision_function`) method (sklearn classifiers do), AND
4. `n_train >= 500` (need enough rows for a stable threshold pick).

If the metric is `roc_auc` or `log_loss`, this skill does NOT apply. If the metric is plain `accuracy` AND classes are balanced (40-60%), the optimal threshold is essentially 0.5 anyway.

## Action
- Generate OOF probability predictions using the same CV split used for hyperparameter selection.
- Sweep `np.linspace(0.20, 0.80, 31)` (or wider for very imbalanced data) and pick the threshold maximizing the headline metric on OOF.
- Apply that threshold to test probs to produce the binary submission.
- Persist `result.json.audit.chosen_threshold`, `chosen_threshold_metric_value`, and the grid.

## Why
H_0/nlp-getting-started: shipped `predict()` at 0.5, OOF F1 0.7592 with P=0.81 / R=0.71. Precision >> recall is the tell that threshold > optimal for F1. Threshold tuning on the same OOF probs (no extra training) typically recovers +0.01-0.03 F1. Free and generalizes to all binary F1/MCC/F-beta tasks.

See skill file for code snippet and cross-task evidence.

# Skill: Train on log1p(target) when the target is right-skewed and non-negative

## Precondition
Apply if ALL of:
1. Regression task (metric rmse/mae/rmsle/mape/r2), AND
2. `(train[target] >= 0).all()`, AND
3. EITHER metric contains `log`/`msle`, OR `train[target].skew() >= 1.0`, OR `train[target].max() / max(1, train[target].median()) >= 20`.

## Action
- Fit on `np.log1p(y)`; predict via `np.clip(np.expm1(model.predict(X)), 0, None)`.
- When metric is RMSLE, log1p-fit with plain MSE loss is exactly the RMSLE objective.
- Always A/B on CV vs raw-y; if raw wins by >1 std keep raw. Persist both in `audit.log_target_ab`.

## Why
H_0/bike-sharing-demand applied log1p (RMSLE metric) and won. H_0/s3e6 (price, RMSE) and s3e9 (strength, RMSE) shipped raw-y models on right-skewed non-negative targets — the A/B was never even attempted. Skill forces it and lets CV decide.

# Skill: Blend predictions from two different model families when CV supports it

## Precondition
Apply if ALL of:
1. `n_train >= 1000`, AND
2. Tabular task (NOT pure text — TF-IDF + linear is its own canonical family), AND
3. Primary model is a GBM, AND
4. Prompt has no latency/size/production tokens (would double inference cost).

## Action
- After tuning the GBM, fit a structurally different family: RF/ExtraTrees (or Ridge/LogReg for the linear bias) on same features.
- OOF for both with the SAME folds; sweep blend weight w ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}; pick by OOF headline.
- If best w ∈ {0, 1}: ship the single model (do not add complexity for nothing).
- Persist `audit.blend_weights` and per-w OOF.

## Why
Every H_0 tabular task shipped a single GBM (same-family seed averaging at best, on s3e9 only). GBM and RF/Ridge have different inductive biases; blending typically gives +0.2-0.8% AUC/accuracy and +1-3% RMSE on right-skewed regression. Skill is bounded (one extra fit, CV-gated, auto-aborts if dominated).

Read `INDEX.md` first to scan skills. Each skill has a precondition you should evaluate against this task; apply only the skills whose preconditions hold.

**Important: iterate over every skill in INDEX.md and mechanically evaluate the precondition** — do not skip skills because you "already have a good plan". For each skill, write one line in `result.json.skills_evaluated_not_applied` (or `skills_applied`) with the explicit reason. Skills you'll commonly miss if you don't iterate: threshold tuning for F1/F-beta metrics (binary classification with a threshold-sensitive metric), log-transforming a skewed non-negative regression target, and blending a GBM with a second model family on tabular tasks. None of these double inference cost meaningfully, all are gated by checkable preconditions, and each is recoverable purely from CV.

# v5 Skill Library — Preconditioned Skills (Harness Optimization Round)

10 conditional skills. The 7 v4 skills are kept; v5 adds 3 modeling skills distilled from H_0 outcomes on 10 train tasks where the solver consistently shipped single-GBM models without threshold tuning or target transforms.

rationale: H_0 results across 10 train tasks show three consistent miss-patterns that no current skill addresses, but each is gated by a cleanly checkable precondition so it generalizes safely to val. (1) nlp-getting-started: binary F1 metric, but the solver called `.predict()` at the implicit 0.5 cutoff and got OOF precision 0.81 / recall 0.71 — the precision-recall imbalance is exactly the signature of a too-high threshold. The new `skill_tune_decision_threshold_for_f1` fires only on threshold-sensitive metrics (F1/F-beta/MCC) and is a no-op for AUC/log-loss/balanced-accuracy tasks. (2) playground-series-s3e6 (Paris-Housing RMSE) and s3e9 (Concrete-Strength RMSE) ship raw-y GBMs on right-skewed non-negative targets without even A/B-testing log1p. The new `skill_log_target_for_skewed_nonnegative_regression` forces the comparison and lets CV decide — it auto-keeps raw-y if it wins on CV, so it cannot regress a task. (3) Every tabular task shipped a single GBM; the new `skill_blend_two_model_families` adds a second family (RF/Ridge), CV-picks a blend weight, and auto-aborts if one model dominates (best weight in {0,1}). All three skills have mechanical preconditions in the v4 style. The solver_prompt edit nudges the solver to systematically iterate over INDEX.md so the new skills aren't silently skipped. The INDEX update documents the additions. Edits are small (3 new files ≤ 100 lines each, one ~5-line solver_prompt change, one INDEX header edit) and total 5 — within budget.
